title: ADA Demand Letter First-Aid Desk
oneLiner: A first-48-hour accessibility lawsuit triage desk that turns a scary demand letter into a prioritized fix packet and lawyer handoff.
targetUser: Small ecommerce owners, one-person businesses, web agencies, and nontechnical founders who receive or fear ADA website accessibility demand letters.
keyUx: Paste the demand letter allegations, site URL, platform, key pages, current widget/scanner status, and deadline; the app maps allegations to WCAG issues, ranks fixes by legal/commerce risk, creates before/after screenshot tasks, and exports a counsel-ready response packet.
searchSignals: EcomBack — ADA Website Accessibility Lawsuits January 2026 Report: https://www.ecomback.com/ada-website-lawsuits-recap-report/january-2026
Reddit r/smallbusiness — one-person business ADA demand letter: https://www.reddit.com/r/smallbusiness/comments/1fegkv3/oneperson_business_demand_letter_for_ada/
stitchPrompt: Design a desktop operations product called ADA Demand Letter First-Aid Desk for small ecommerce owners, one-person businesses, web agencies, and nontechnical founders who receive or fear ADA website accessibility demand letters. Users should paste demand-letter allegations, site URL, platform, key revenue pages, current accessibility widget/scanner status, deadline, and developer notes, then map allegations to WCAG issues, rank fixes by legal and commerce risk, create before/after screenshot tasks, and export a counsel-ready response packet. Include a demand-letter intake, allegation-to-WCAG mapper, top-page risk scanner, overlay/widget reality check, 48-hour fix queue, developer screenshot evidence board, and lawyer handoff packet export. Design direction: use an operator-dense aesthetic with compact legal-risk chips, split-pane allegation cards, dense remediation checklists, evidence thumbnails, and a calm red-to-green triage rail so the product feels like an emergency command desk for a panicked small business, not a generic accessibility scanner.
